analysis:
Examined docs/reference/configuration.md BASE lines 1–484 and the supplied change map/partial patch against the canonical index and detailed T-041 definition. Within these numbered excerpts, only the update date (line 3) changes; the documented GLM admission/retirement, encrypted prefix-cache activation, App Attest qualification, logout, lifecycle, model-cache selection and scheduler controls are unchanged. No concrete security regression is established by these units; pre-existing cache timing risk is not a new finding.
The partial patch at BASE 920 onward introduces release-supplied cluster_runtime facts from which an accepting coordinator derives cluster approvals, pair-serving grants and parity qualifications. This is security-relevant to A-005, A-011, A-017, T-054 and T-056: release publication must not silently substitute for independently approved qualification or turn build declarations into proof of correct computation. The full changed documentation and corresponding release registration, coordinator approval policy, and member-side validation are absent from this source scope. Integration must reconcile this new contract with the canonical qualification separation, verify who can authorize the block and its grants, and examine remaining changed ranges (BASE 923–1573 / HEAD 923–1636). The bounded patch alone does not establish a missing control or implementation regression.
